title: Regional fuse playbook: control-plane drain and SLO-aware tenant eviction
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Define and implement a regional 'fuse' and playbook that lets us safely isolate a Dedicated/Private control plane (or subset of tenants) for upgrades, incidents, or region-level failover. The feature combines circuit-breaker semantics at the routing layer, SLO-aware tenant eviction/drain logic, and a graceful load-shedding ladder to protect healthy regions and preserve critical customer SLAs.
background: We run Dedicated and Private control planes that must be isolatable for air-gapped upgrades, emergency maintenance, and region-level failures. Current approaches either do blunt tenant quarantines (high customer pain) or momentary overloads (SLO breaches). We need a predictable, testable mechanism that: 1) contains failure domains, 2) performs minimal-impact draining and fallback, and 3) ties to SLO budgets to inform eviction order and throttles.
goals: 1) Prevent noisy upgrades or tenant hot-spots in one region from causing cascading SLO violations elsewhere. 2) Provide a deterministic, low-risk upgrade path for control-plane components in Dedicated/Private deployments. 3) Implement an SLO-aware eviction policy that favors low-impact routing and preserves critical tenant availability.
success_metrics: - Reduce cross-region SLO violations during control-plane upgrades by >= 90% in canary tests. - Decrease mean customer-visible error rate during targeted isolation exercises to < 0.2%. - Complete controlled isolation cycle (drain, upgrade, restore) with no manual rollback in 95% of runs.
approach: 1) Circuit-fuse: add a region-aware circuit-breaker at the global routing proxy that can open on per-tenant or per-tenant-group signals. 2) SLO-budgeted eviction: maintain per-tenant error/latency budgets; eviction priority computed from composition of budget burn, request criticality, and contractual tier. 3) Graceful drain: implement a staged drain sequence with KV cache flush, in-flight request draining, and fallback routing to compatible model variants or alternate regions. 4) Orchestration hooks: control-plane APIs to schedule fences, set drain windows, and attach human-verification steps for high-risk tenants.
design_decisions: - Use tokenized tenant affinity metadata in the router so we can make decisions without querying control-plane state for every request (latency-sensitive). - Eviction priority will be computed by combining 'SLO burn' (30%), 'tier weight' (40%), and 'statefulness' fingerprint (30%). - We will prefer model-variant fallback rather than cross-region failover when the estimated tail-latency impact is below threshold. - Default behavior: automated drills in staging, manual gating for production until M=3 successful dry-runs.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Prefetching tenant metadata into the routing plane increases memory and cache invalidation complexity. - Over-aggressive eviction risks violating contractual SLAs; under-aggressive eviction risks cascading failures. - Fallback to alternate regions increases egress and inter-region latency/cost; must be balanced by cost controls.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Router circuit-fuse prototype (feature flag) + per-tenant SLO budget store (in-memory + persisted checkpoint). Phase 2: Implement staged drain sequence and model-variant fallback logic. Phase 3: End-to-end canary in partner Dedicated cluster, run chaos tests and SLO burn simulations. Phase 4: Gradual rollout with policy templates for customer tiers.
rollout_plan: - Week 1: Deploy router feature flag to staging. - Week 2: Run synthetic tenant isolation exercises; validate SLO impact. - Week 3-4: Canary in one low-risk Dedicated customer region with manual ops supervision. - Week 5: After two successful canaries and postmortem, enable manual-trigger in production. - Post-rollout: Add automated periodic drills and two-step approval for high-impact tenants.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for eviction ordering and ordering invariants. - Integration tests: simulate 10k qps tenant spike while issuing control-plane upgrade to ensure fuses open. - Chaos experiments: shutdown region control-plane process, assert that routing isolates the region without >1% SLO regression in healthy regions. - Game days with platform teams and 2 partner customers.
monitoring_and_runbook: - Dashboards: per-tenant SLO burn, fuse state, active drains, cross-region error rate. - Alerts: fuse_opened, drain_stalled, fallback_failed, cross_region_SLO_gain. - Runbook steps: 1) triage alert -> check dashboard, 2) if fuse opened intentionally, validate drain progress and customer notifications, 3) if accidental, run immediate rollback: close fuse, rehydrate routing cache, and escalate to oncall control-plane. - Post-incident analysis template to capture timing and decision points.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike complete. Router prototype can flip per-tenant fuse with TTL; initial perf impact +0.4% median latency.
2026-02-26: SLO budget store design reviewed. Decided on hybrid in-memory checkpointing to reduce control-plane reads.
2026-03-03: Design review with Security and Privacy. KMS integration required for tenant metadata at rest. Security requested additional audit events for any automated eviction.
2026-03-08: Integration branch created: routing/fuse-proto. Added feature-flag gating and basic metrics for open/close events. PR opened: #5123.
2026-03-12: Canary plan approved by SRE and Product. First controlled canary scheduled for 2026-03-18 in partner Dedicated region (eu-west-2-low-risk).
2026-03-12: Blockers: need ephemeral capacity reservation for canary window (ticket infra-ephemeral-332). Ops to provision by 2026-03-16.
review_feedback: PM (Sofie Nilsson): Ensure customer notification templates are ready before any production isolation. Add a 'quiet period' post-restoration to validate no latent errors.
SRE (Daniel Cho): Prefer conservative defaults for eviction thresholds; require two sequential budget burns before eviction candidate promotion.
Design (Lina Gomez): Add UX surface in Console to show 'fuse state' and expected customer impact for each tenant during a drain window.
Security (Ravi Kapoor): Mandate audit events for any automatic eviction; record operator id and policy version.
next_steps: Finish persistence layer for SLO budgets and add encryption-at-rest as per Security feedback.
Implement drain progress ETA and per-tenant rollback hooks.
Run two dry-run evacuations in staging and capture SLO graphs for postmortem.
Coordinate with Sales/CS to prepare customer comms templates for canary and production drills.
notes: This ticket coordinates closely with routing and control-plane teams; it is intentionally cross-cutting and will require paired oncall coverage during canaries.
We will track cost delta for fallback routes separately and propose a cost-recovery billing metric for cross-region egress used during forced failovers.
